senses.sense_definition: A system of taxation where the tax rate decreases as the taxable amount increases, or a system of progressive decreases in rates.

examples.text: The government implemented a system of <w>degression</w> to lower the tax burden on high-income earners.
Economic analysts debated whether the proposed <w>degression</w> of tariffs would stimulate international trade.

senses.sense_definition: A method of varying the level of detail in a description based on the importance of the subject or available space.

examples.text: The librarian used <w>degression</w> to provide shorter summaries for less significant historical documents.
Applying <w>degression</w> to the cataloging process ensures that key works receive the most thorough descriptions.

senses.sense_definition: The act of descending or moving downward.

examples.text: The slow <w>degression</w> of the mountain path made the descent much safer for the hikers.
Observers watched the steady <w>degression</w> of the hot air balloon toward the landing field.

traits.comment: This term is rarely used in modern English to describe physical descent.

examples.text: In older manuscripts, one might encounter the word <w>degression</w> used where we now write digression.
The author's frequent <w>degression</w> from the main plot was a common stylistic choice in that era.

traits.comment: This spelling is no longer in standard use.
